answer: Since the forge escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the sonnet audit releases each pair. A farm running 168 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the falcon graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. Admission needs 3 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
